key_insight: PEACE improves adult-to-pediatric ECG transfer by using diagnosis-aware, label-conditioned cross-modal alignment instead of global waveform-text fusion.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical pretraining strategy for clinical ECG systems when pediatric labels are scarce, while still requiring only ECG input at inference.
method: Composes only positive-label diagnosis descriptors into axis tokens and a fused knowledge embedding.
Uses a label query network to cross-attend diagnostic labels over ECG tokens and axis tokens.
Applies label-set-aware bidirectional contrastive learning with curriculum adaptive fusion during training.
evidence_signal: On ZZU-pECG, PEACE achieved macro-average AUCs of 59.39% zero-shot, 81.74% at 50-shot, and 91.56% with full fine-tuning, and reached 96.90% macro-average AUC on PTB-XL after fine-tuning.
watch_item: The knowledge branch is training-only, so gains depend on high-quality label text and may be sensitive to label harmonization across datasets.
paper_title: Knowledge-Guided Cross-Modal Fusion for Adult-to-Pediatric ECG Transfer via Label-Conditioned Contrastive Alignment
